Thesis overview

Generative modeling for embodied communicative behaviors: speech and gesture generation

PhD thesis · Supplementary material

Téo Guichoux

Institution
ISIR - IRCAM, Sorbonne University
Degree
PhD in Computer Science
Supervisors
Catherine Pelachaud, Nicolas Obin, Laure Soulier
Year
2026
Defense
November 24th 2026

Abstract

Human communication is inherently multimodal, with speech and co-speech gestures closely coordinated in time and meaning. This thesis investigates unified generative models that produce both modalities jointly, rather than relying on separate speech and gesture pipelines.

We first introduce Gelina, a discrete autoregressive model that represents speech and gestures as interleaved token sequences. We then propose Gaspard, a continuous autoregressive diffusion model that operates on temporally aligned latent representations and uses modality-decoupled classifier-free guidance to improve gesture dynamics and expressivity.

Beyond conventional evaluations, the thesis also studies the communicative properties of generated behaviors, including gesture categories, speech–gesture synchrony, and higher-level organization. The results show that unified models can generate diverse, coordinated speech and gestures with meaningful temporal and semantic relationships.
